questions.q: To preserve peace, the article says Islam lays down one rule for the individual and one for society. What are they?
options: Study for the individual; trade for society
Not quite. The article says: Patience for the individual; no offensive war for society.
Wealth for the individual; power for society
Not quite. The article says: Patience for the individual; no offensive war for society.
Silence for the individual; strict laws for society
Not quite. The article says: Patience for the individual; no offensive war for society.
Patience for the individual; no offensive war for society
Yes. Only defence is permitted, and that conditionally.
questions.rationale: “One, at the individual level, stresses the exercise of patience, and the other, at the social level, forbids taking the offensive.”

questions.q: “The sun is not allowed to overtake the moon… Each in its own orbit runs.” How does the article relate this to human beings?
options: Man’s life is fixed like a planet’s
Not quite. The article says: The universe keeps to the path of peace by law; man must adopt the same path by his own free choice.
Day and night are equal for all
Not quite. The article says: The universe keeps to the path of peace by law; man must adopt the same path by his own free choice.
Man should study astronomy
Not quite. The article says: The universe keeps to the path of peace by law; man must adopt the same path by his own free choice.
The universe keeps to the path of peace by law; man must adopt the same path by his own free choice
Well read. Peace is built into nature.
questions.rationale: “The law of nature is imposed upon universe by God, whereas man has to adopt this path of peace of his own free will.”

questions.q: A man lamented to George Bernard Shaw that his community was backward in education, though he himself was unschooled. What did Shaw advise?
options: To write to the newspapers about it
Not quite. The article says: To get an education himself first, so that at least one person would no longer be uneducated.
To move to another country
Not quite. The article says: To get an education himself first, so that at least one person would no longer be uneducated.
To get an education himself first, so that at least one person would no longer be uneducated
Right. Fill the gap by starting with yourself.
To raise money for a school
Not quite. The article says: To get an education himself first, so that at least one person would no longer be uneducated.
questions.rationale: “Shaw advised him to secure education for himself first so that at least one person in the community shall no longer remain illiterate.”

questions.q: What does the article mean by saying a good citizen has a “predictable character”?
options: He is easy to persuade
Not quite. The article says: Others can rely on his conduct beforehand, as a gardener trusts that no one will harm his saplings.
Others can rely on his conduct beforehand, as a gardener trusts that no one will harm his saplings
Yes. Trust makes shared life possible.
He does the same things every day
Not quite. The article says: Others can rely on his conduct beforehand, as a gardener trusts that no one will harm his saplings.
He never changes his opinions
Not quite. The article says: Others can rely on his conduct beforehand, as a gardener trusts that no one will harm his saplings.
questions.rationale: “A good citizen is one who has a predictable character. His fellow human beings should be confident of his behaviour beforehand.”

questions.q: The article says discovering God is “much more than just acquiring a dry creed.” What is it, then?
options: Learning a set of definitions
Not quite. The article says: A living experience that fills heart and mind with light and changes the person.
Completing certain rituals
Not quite. The article says: A living experience that fills heart and mind with light and changes the person.
Joining a group of believers
Not quite. The article says: A living experience that fills heart and mind with light and changes the person.
A living experience that fills heart and mind with light and changes the person
Well reasoned. One cannot find the source of all beauty and stay unmoved.
questions.rationale: “It means filling one’s heart and soul with the radiant glow of divine light and opening one’s mind to incredible beauty and delicacy.”

questions.q: Why does the article say that believing in God is similar to believing in one’s own self?
options: Because neither can be doubted by anyone
Not quite. The article says: Each of us knows himself as a conscious being with will and power; God is such a Being on an infinitely greater scale.
Because both beliefs are taught in childhood
Not quite. The article says: Each of us knows himself as a conscious being with will and power; God is such a Being on an infinitely greater scale.
Each of us knows himself as a conscious being with will and power; God is such a Being on an infinitely greater scale
Correct. “Man himself is ample evidence for himself.”
Because man is part of God
Not quite. The article says: Each of us knows himself as a conscious being with will and power; God is such a Being on an infinitely greater scale.
questions.rationale: “Since our experience of such a being is an everyday matter, what is astonishing about the existence of God, who also is a being wielding personal power, although on a scale far greater than ourselves?”

questions.q: What does the article call the only way to build a non-violent society?
options: Changing the thinking of the individual through education, since violence begins in the mind
Right. Long work, but there is no alternative.
Waiting for a great leader
Not quite. The article says: Changing the thinking of the individual through education, since violence begins in the mind.
Passing stricter laws
Not quite. The article says: Changing the thinking of the individual through education, since violence begins in the mind.
Separating communities from one another
Not quite. The article says: Changing the thinking of the individual through education, since violence begins in the mind.
questions.rationale: “There is only one way of exploiting the nonviolent method for the reform of a society—and that is, to bring about a change in the thinking of the individual.”

options: In ancient kingdoms, showing lost wisdom
Not quite. The article says: In the natural world, which runs with perfect precision – pointing to an all-powerful, perfect Creator.
Nowhere at all, showing that order is an illusion
Not quite. The article says: In the natural world, which runs with perfect precision – pointing to an all-powerful, perfect Creator.
In the natural world, which runs with perfect precision – pointing to an all-powerful, perfect Creator
Yes. Sunrise can be predicted years ahead.

Not quite. The article says: In the natural world, which runs with perfect precision – pointing to an all-powerful, perfect Creator.
questions.rationale: “In the natural world established and managed by God, zero-defect management prevails fully… we realize that there is a Creator of this universe who is All-Powerful and Perfect.”

questions.q: A famous writer on health hoped to reach a hundred and then return to do other work, but died at eighty-nine. What does the article observe from this?
options: Human ambitions exceed one earthly life; their fulfilment lies in the eternal world, for which one must prepare
Well read. This world cannot hold all our dreams.
Health advice is of little use
Not quite. The article says: Human ambitions exceed one earthly life; their fulfilment lies in the eternal world, for which one must prepare.
Ambition is always harmful
Not quite. The article says: Human ambitions exceed one earthly life; their fulfilment lies in the eternal world, for which one must prepare.
People should plan to live longer
Not quite. The article says: Human ambitions exceed one earthly life; their fulfilment lies in the eternal world, for which one must prepare.
questions.rationale: “Sometimes his ambitions in this world are so far-reaching that they cannot even be fulfilled in a life span of 100 years… he will be raised up in an eternal world of infinite opportunities.”

questions.q: “Repel evil with what is better; then you will see that one who was once your enemy has become your dearest friend.” What does the commentary call the greatest strength of one who calls to truth?
options: A large following
Not quite. The article says: Treating people well even when they do not – patient, one-sided good conduct.
Readiness to answer in kind
Not quite. The article says: Treating people well even when they do not – patient, one-sided good conduct.
Skill in argument
Not quite. The article says: Treating people well even when they do not – patient, one-sided good conduct.
Treating people well even when they do not – patient, one-sided good conduct
Exactly. It persuades where retaliation cannot.
questions.rationale: “The greatest weapon of a preacher of Truth is his ability to treat people well. Even if people are not good to him, he should be good to them.”
